Day 31 of 100 · Infrastructure Automation

Ansible Facts

#100DaysOfCloudAndSecurityInfrastructure AutomationPublished journey entry

Facts let automation discover the host it is operating on instead of hard-coding assumptions about every machine.

Architecture / mental model

setup / fact gathering → ansible_facts → condition / template / task decision

How it works

Fact gathering exposes operating-system, network, memory, architecture and other host information as structured variables.

Facts allow one playbook to branch appropriately across distributions or use discovered interface and filesystem information without separate copies of the automation.

Gather only what you need when scale or performance matters. Facts are useful because they make automation adapt to reality, not because more data is automatically better.

Hands-on reference

ansible all -i inventory.ini -m setup
ansible all -i inventory.ini -m setup -a 'filter=ansible_distribution*'

Verification

Compare selected facts with host commands such as `/etc/os-release`, `ip addr` or `uname` in a lab to understand what the fact represents.

Field note / gotcha

Facts describe the host Ansible reached, which is another reason correct inventory targeting matters. The wrong server can provide perfectly valid facts.

Security considerations

Facts may expose interface, hostname and system metadata; handle logs and artifacts accordingly in sensitive environments.

What I learned

Good automation observes before it assumes.
